header.sector: Memory (DRAM, HBM, NAND): supply, pricing, capacity
header.title: High DRAM prices push budget smartphone brands to adopt cheaper reballed memory

s01_bottom_line.text: TrendForce estimates reballed memory penetration in smartphones at ~3-4% in 2026, potentially 7-9% in 2027, as brands use it to offset rising mobile DRAM contract prices, especially in sub-CNY1,299 4G phones. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩

The article frames reballed memory as a cost-management workaround that nonetheless leaves the upward DRAM contract price trend intact, with potential spread into higher price segments if prices keep climbing in 1Q27.

A rising DRAM price cycle is strong enough that budget smartphone makers increasingly substitute reballed (reused) memory, but the article says this will not derail the upward DRAM price trend, so the main read-through is continued memory pricing strength.

LPDDR4X 4GB accounts for the bulk of available reballed memory, used mostly in 4G smartphones priced below CNY 1,299.
Increasing reballed memory use is unlikely to significantly disrupt the upward trend in DRAM contract prices.
